html:
The Battle of Kursk was fought from 5 July to 23 August 1943 around Kursk in western Russia. The Red Army stopped the last big German offensive in the east and then went over to the attack. It included the largest tank battles in history.

After Stalingrad the front had a large bulge around Kursk. Germany planned to cut it off from north and south. Hitler delayed the attack to wait for new Tiger and Panther tanks. The Soviet command knew what was coming and chose to defend first. It dug belt after belt of trenches, minefields and anti-tank guns. About 780,000 Germans with nearly 3,000 tanks attacked 1.9 million Soviet troops with about 5,000. In the north they advanced about 12 km. In the south they got about 35 km, as far as a huge tank fight at Prokhorovka on 12 July. Then Hitler stopped the attack; the Allies had just landed in Sicily.

Soviet counter-attacks took Orel and Kharkiv by late August. Soviet losses were several times the German, but Germany could not make good its own. It never again attacked in strength in the east. The Red Army advanced across Ukraine and, by 1945, to Berlin.
